mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% within the last month signals a tightening monetary policy, which increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate investments, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS increased by more than 0.5% in the last month.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate by more than 0.3% within the last month indicates a tightening labor market, which increases consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative in > 60% of instances where UNRATE decreased by more than 0.3% in the last month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real estate sales (HOUST) by more than 5% over the last two months signals increased consumer confidence and economic activity, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in > 60% of instances where HOUST increased by more than 5% in the last two months.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% over the last two months signals a reduction in supply-side capacity, which can lead to increased prices and reduced corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances where INDPRO decreased by more than 1% in the last two months.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 200,000 over the last month signals strong labor market conditions, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in > 60% of instances where PAYEMS increased by more than 200,000 in the last month.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4% and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.5% in the last month, it indicates inflationary pressure coupled with high borrowing costs, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 4% and CPIAUCSL increase > 0.5% in 1 month
regime_hint: inflationary pressure with high interest rates
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS > 4% and CPIAUCSL increased by more than 0.5% in the last month.

mechanism_narrative: When real GDP (GDPC1) grows by more than 2% quarter-over-quarter and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases by more than 0.3% in the last month, it signals strong economic growth and a tightening labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 increase > 2% QoQ and UNRATE decrease > 0.3% in 1 month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in > 60% of instances where GDPC1 increased by more than 2% QoQ and UNRATE decreased by more than 0.3% in the last month.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) increases by more than 1% over the last two months and real estate sales (HOUST) increase by more than 5% in the same period, it signals a strong supply-side and demand-side economic expansion, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO increase > 1% and HOUST increase > 5% in 2 months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in > 60% of instances where INDPRO increased by more than 1% and HOUST increased by more than 5% in the last two months.
